Executive Summary In 2022, Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) launched “Net Zero by 2031,” outlining plans to reduce Massport-controlled sources of emissions through operational improvements and sustainable infrastructure (Massport 2025b). They plan to achieve these goals through energy conservation and efficiency, enabling renewable energy resources, and alternative ground transportation. Massport established 2019 data as their baseline year, at which time Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) represented roughly 92% of the 877,947 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (Massport 2025c). Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is a commercially available drop-in fuel made from biomass and waste feedstocks and is chemically identical to and meets the same fuel quality specifications as Jet A. SAF can be used in the same infrastructure and aircraft as Jet A. SAF can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 90% and is a key and is a key near-term technology for aviation to reduce emissions (Prussi et al. 2021). This study assesses the technical and economic potential for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production and use across New England. Massport launched a Massachusetts and New England Regional SAF Hub in June 2025 to unite industries and sectors for the purpose of developing strategies, partnerships, and policy frameworks to accelerate SAF adoption (Massport 2025a).
